Mechanistic Interpretability · Research Report

Probe-guided attribution & control of sycophancy in language models

Can we locate where a model decides to flatter the user, read that decision from its activations, and then intervene to switch it off — without degrading the model?

GPT-2 · Pythia-410M · Qwen2.5-Instruct Anthropic sycophancy evals probes · patching · steering · capping

01Research aim

Aim

To convert a readable internal representation of sycophancy into a causal lever — an intervention that reliably changes the model's answer from sycophantic to honest, while preserving its general capabilities.

Sycophancy — telling the user what they want to hear rather than what is true — is a safety-relevant behavior. If it corresponds to a direction or region in activation space, we should be able to both detect it and switch it off. This report tests how far that program actually gets.

02Research questions

  1. Is a model's sycophancy preference linearly decodable from its activations, and where?
  2. Is that signal real, or a trivial surface-feature / format confound?
  3. Does sycophancy differ between base and instruction-tuned models (pre- vs post-training)?
  4. Are the most decodable layers also the most causal ones?
  5. Can we intervene to flip sycophantic answers — and does control come cleanly?

03Data & methods

Data. Anthropic's model-written sycophancy evaluations — real, published data — pooling three subsets (philosophy, NLP-researcher, and political opinions) into ~300 prompts. Each prompt states a persona's view and offers a sycophantic answer (agrees with the persona) and an honest answer (the correct/neutral view).

Target — behavior margin. Rather than a hand label, we use the model's own preference, measured as average per-token log-probability:

behavior_margin = avg logP(sycophantic answer | prompt) − avg logP(honest answer | prompt)

Positive → the model leans sycophantic; negative → honest.

Probe. A linear probe reads the activation at the final prompt token — the instant before the model answers — and predicts the behavior margin. If it succeeds, the sycophancy decision is encoded in the activations before a single answer-token is produced.

Interventions. Contrastive patching (paste an opposite-preference prompt's activation in), probe steering (add α·direction), and activation capping (clip the projection onto the direction), with mean-ablation as a baseline. Headline metric: targeted syc→honest answer-flip rate, plus a side-effect score from generation on basic prompts. All estimates carry bootstrap 95% CIs.

Correctness note. Building the controls exposed a truncation bug — long prompts (~170 tokens) were cut at 128, zeroing 88% of margins and faking a "7% sycophancy rate." After fixing (max_length = 256), sycophancy is ~50% and all results below are on the corrected data.

04Experiments & results

Exp 1Is sycophancy decodable, and where?
Aim
Test whether a linear probe can predict the behavior margin from prompt-final activations, layer by layer, in two model families.
Method
Train per-layer ridge probes on prompt-final activations → behavior_margin; report held-out test Pearson vs relative depth for GPT-2 and Pythia-410M.
Observation. Sycophancy preference is decodable and the signal strengthens with depth — with the same rising shape in two unrelated architectures, evidence of a real shared mechanism (GPT-2 peaks 0.52, Pythia 0.61).
Exp 2Is it real, or a surface-feature confound?
Aim
Rule out that the probe is just reading prompt format (e.g. the phrase “do you agree?”) or length.
Method
Re-run the identical probe pipeline on control targets: a random-label probe (shuffled target = noise floor), surface-feature probes, and a topic probe.
Observation. There is real signal above noise (0.52 vs a 0.25 random-label floor), but surface features are trivially decodable (up to 1.0) — so a confound contribution cannot be fully excluded at this sample size.
Exp 3Base vs. instruction-tuned models
Aim
Test whether sycophancy is amplified by post-training (instruction tuning) rather than present only in base models.
Method
Compute sycophancy rate (fraction of prompts with behavior_margin > 0) for base GPT-2, base Pythia-410M, and Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct.
Observation. The instruction-tuned model is more sycophantic (66% vs ~50%), consistent with post-training amplifying sycophancy. Caveat: cross-family comparison — the clean test is a single model's base→SFT→DPO→instruct staged checkpoints.
Exp 4Decodability vs. causal effect, per layer
Aim
Test the reviewer's key point: are the most decodable layers also the strongest layers to intervene on?
Method
For every layer, measure decodability (test Pearson) and causal effect (behavior_margin change when that layer's residual is patched), with bootstrap CIs.
Observation. The peak-decodable layer (≈8) is not the peak-causal layer (≈1) — reading and moving the behavior live in different places. This reframes the whole intervention strategy: target causal layers, not readable ones.
Exp 5Can we flip the answer at causal layers?
Aim
Test whether targeting high-causal layers gives stronger answer-level control than decodable or random layers.
Method
Apply contrastive patching / steering / capping at causal-topk vs decodable-topk vs random layers; measure targeted syc→honest flip rate across an intervention-strength sweep.
Observation. At gentle strengths, no layer choice controls the answer. But under a stronger sweep, steering the causal layers flips up to 83% of sycophantic answers, where decodable-layer targeting gives ~0 — so causal-layer targeting is actionable.
Exp 6Does control break the model?
Aim
Check the reviewer's caution: if an intervention reduces sycophancy, does it also harm general capability?
Method
Generate on basic prompts (“Why is the sky blue?”, “What is 2+2?”) with and without the flip-producing intervention; score weirdness, repetition, length ratio, and basic-QA drop.
Observation. The answer-flip comes at a high cost: side-effect score 0.66 (the model becomes weird and repetitive). Control here reflects general disruption, not a clean sycophancy switch.
Exp 7Is there a clean operating point?
Aim
Search for any intervention configuration that achieves meaningful control with low side effects.
Method
Grid over layer-selection × direction × intervention × strength; score each by targeted flip and side-effect; plot the control-vs-harm trade-off (Pareto).
Observation. The Pareto front has no top-left point: strong control comes with disruption; clean interventions (capping) produce ~0 flips. A capability-preserving lever was not found in GPT-2 at these settings.

05Key observations

0.52 / 0.61
peak probe decodability (GPT-2 / Pythia) — replicated across families
66% vs ~50%
sycophancy rate: instruct vs base models
L8 ≠ L1
peak-decodable layer ≠ peak-causal layer
0.83 / 0.66
answer-flip achievable, but at a high side-effect cost
  • Decodable and replicated. Sycophancy preference is linearly readable, rises with depth, and shows the same shape in GPT-2 and Pythia.
  • Signal is real but not clean. It clears the random-label floor, yet surface features are also highly decodable — confounds aren't fully excluded.
  • Post-training matters. The instruction-tuned model is more sycophantic than base models.
  • Decoding ≠ causation. The most readable layer is not the most causal one — the central methodological finding.
  • Control is reachable, not clean. Steering causal layers flips most answers, but only by disrupting the model; clean interventions flip nothing.

06Conclusion

Bottom line. We can read a model's sycophancy preference well, and it strengthens with depth and replicates across models. We can even flip most sycophantic answers by steering the high-causal layers — but only at strengths that also break the model. Reliable, capability-preserving causal control is not yet achieved.

This is a well-instrumented result rather than an overclaim: decodability is established with controls and replication; the causal claim is bounded with answer-flip metrics, side-effect checks, and bootstrap CIs. The gap between "readable" and "controllable" is now the sharp, open research question.

07Next steps

  1. HuggingFace steering on instruct models. Implement residual hooks for Qwen/Gemma so the causal question can be tested where sycophancy is a genuine learned behavior.
  2. OLMo staged checkpoints. Base → SFT → DPO → instruct of one model — the clean, confound-free test of whether sycophancy is pre- or post-training in origin.
  3. Sycophancy as a subspace. A single linear lever may be inherently limited; cap/steer within a low-rank subspace to seek control without the coherence collapse.
  4. Fine trade-off search. Sweep capping strength and steering strength densely to confirm whether a capability-preserving operating point exists at all.
